archetype.name: Game Manager (high-volume)
archetype.definition: A veteran short-to-intermediate distributor who wins by getting the ball out on time and keeping sacks down, now asked to throw 40 times a game because his defense keeps putting Arizona behind.

report.headline: A sound short-and-middle passer whose volume is bought by Arizona's leaking defense
report.take:
Brissett is what he has been for most of a decade: a big, calm pocket passer who works the short and intermediate field and seldom creates beyond the design. His career intended depth has stayed between 7.1 and 9.1 air yards every season, and his best year by efficiency, 2022 in Cleveland, came when he paired that range with accuracy (CPOE 2.888, 7th). This year's 7.38 intended air yards and 2.63-second time to throw fit that history. His -0.034 EPA per dropback ranks 28th of 45, which is roughly what he is: a little below average, not a liability on any given snap.

The box score is driven by volume, not efficiency. He is attempting 40.3 passes a game for a 2-5 team whose defense ranks 31st against the pass and 31st in explosive passes allowed, so Arizona is chasing points most weeks. That is how a 5.67 yards-per-attempt passer (40th of 45) gets to 228.6 yards a game and a 3,886-yard pace. His yards per attempt is down 1.27 from last year and his yards per game are down 51.9. The staff has also changed his process: the ball comes out 0.31 seconds faster than in 2025, his bad-throw rate fell from 16.7% to 11% (8th of 38), and his aggressiveness into tight windows jumped 8 points to 24.47%.

The splits show where the value is made and where it leaks. Throws of 10 to 19 air yards are excellent: 0.521 EPA per attempt, 27.6 EPA in total, 2 TDs and no picks. Throws over the middle add 17.4. Then it falls apart. Deep balls have a 19.2% completion rate, -17.9 CPOE and 3 interceptions on 26 attempts. Screens and throws behind the line have cost 16.3 EPA. Third down has cost 32.5 with a 29.8% conversion rate. The game-state split is the one that matters most: he is +0.163 EPA per play when trailing by 9 or more and -0.147 within one score, and -0.625 in close fourth quarters. Much of his production arrives once the game has tilted away from Arizona.

The outlook is stable but low-ceiling. The role is secure: he has taken 100% of snaps every week, and Carson Beck is hurt. Trey McBride (0.244 EPA per target on 78 targets) is a reliable outlet, and the defense will keep forcing volume. Expect steady 15-ish PPR games with a few spikes in shootouts. The interceptions will keep coming as long as he keeps throwing deep into a 3-INT, 19% completion bucket.

strengths.title: Intermediate middle of the field
strengths.body: His 10-to-19-yard throws are among the most productive throws in the offense, and the middle of the field carries his passing game. This is timing-and-anticipation work from the pocket, which matches what he did in his better years. With 53 attempts the sample is moderate, but it fits his skill set and should stay a positive.

strengths.title: Cleaner, quicker process than 2025
strengths.body: The ball comes out faster, and his bad-throw rate dropped sharply from last year to 8th of 38. His sack rate of 5.1% sits below the league average of 6.7%. The faster release is a scheme choice that should hold. The accuracy gain is partly real, though his overall CPOE (0.15) remains middling.

strengths.title: The McBride connection
strengths.body: McBride has drawn 78 targets at 0.244 EPA each, the only high-volume target adding real value. A tight end who wins underneath and up the seam suits Brissett's range. That makes McBride a dependable floor for him regardless of matchup.

concerns.title: Wins garbage time, loses close games
concerns.body: He is efficient when trailing by two scores and below water when the game is still in doubt, especially in close fourth quarters. Third down has been a sinkhole: no TDs, 4 INTs and under 30% conversions facing long distances. These are the snaps that decide games, and they explain a 2-5 record better than his yardage does. This is a real limitation, consistent with a career of sub-.500 records.

concerns.title: The deep ball isn't there
concerns.body: He completes about one in five throws of 20+ air yards, with 3 interceptions and a CPOE near -18. His career aDOT has never strayed far from 8 yards, so this is who he is, not bad luck. The new aggressiveness makes it costlier; his 45.7% aggressiveness game against the Giants produced 3 picks and -18.2 EPA. The fix is to throw deep less, not to expect better results on those throws.

concerns.title: Volume depends on a bad defense
concerns.body: His yardage rank, 20th per game, is far better than his efficiency rank, 40th in yards per attempt. That gap is game script: Arizona's pass defense is among the worst in the league. If the defense steadies, his attempts and yardage fall with it, because his per-play profile can't carry the numbers alone.

trend.note: His game EPA has swung between +10.1 and -18.2 with no lasting pattern, alternating usable and poor weeks. The last three games are a hair better per dropback than his season (-0.02) on more volume (260.7 yards a game), but CPOE slipped to -1.2.

nextGame.headline: Dallas's soft underneath defense and weak rush suit his game
nextGame.body:
This is close to his ideal setup. Dallas ranks 30th in defensive EPA and 30th against the pass, and it is 31st on short throws, exactly where Brissett lives. Its 27th-ranked sack rate and 29th-ranked hit rate mean his quick release should face little disruption. The one part of Dallas's defense that holds up is deep passing (13th), which is the zone he should avoid anyway. The Book has Arizona as a 6.5-point underdog in a 54.5 total, against a Dallas offense ranked 4th in EPA. That points to another game where he is throwing a lot from behind, which is when his numbers look best.

On Arizona's side, guard Jon Gaines (60% of snaps) is out, which thins an interior line that already ranks 23rd in hit rate allowed. Jeremiyah Love was expected to practice Wednesday. His return would give the offense more of a run game, though Dallas tends to get run on (offenses pass 4.8 points less than normal against it). Jalen Brooks's season-ending surgery costs little, given his -0.209 EPA per target. For Dallas, linebacker Dee Winters (61% of snaps) is out and Marist Liufau is on IR, as of reports from their Monday game. Missing linebackers weaken the coverage over the middle and on tight ends that McBride works.

keyMatchups.title: McBride against depleted linebackers
keyMatchups.body: Dallas has allowed 0.61 EPA per target to opposing top tight ends, 30th in the league, and is now without Winters and Liufau. McBride is Brissett's most productive target and works the middle, where Brissett has done his best work. Expect a heavy dose of him.

keyMatchups.title: Short game versus short defense
keyMatchups.body: Dallas allows 0.23 EPA on short passes, 31st, and Brissett completes 75% of his 0-to-9-yard throws. The quick game should move the chains, and could even help on third down, where he has struggled.

keyMatchups.title: Shootout script
keyMatchups.body: A 54.5 total pairs Dallas's 4th-ranked offense with Arizona's 31st-ranked pass defense. Brissett is +0.163 EPA per play when trailing by two scores, so a lopsided game helps his line even if it hurts Arizona.

nextGame.watch: Whether he keeps shots downfield in check against the one part of Dallas's defense that holds up, or gives away a deep interception in a game the short game should win.

restOfSeason.body:
The volume is the sustainable part. The 100% snap share, the 40-plus attempts and Arizona's pass defense all look stable, so 220 to 260 yards a game is a reasonable baseline. His efficiency should stay around league-average-minus: his career shows no sign of a deep game emerging, and the third-down and close-game struggles match a long run of losing records. Ten TDs against six INTs is close to what his volume and modest TD rate (3.5%) earn, with no obvious regression either way. The interception count could tick down if the staff dials back the new aggressiveness.

Upside comes from soft matchups and shootouts like Dallas, where a 260-to-290-yard, two-touchdown game is realistic. The downside is games against strong defenses, like Seattle and Denver, that collapse the short game. Love's return would help the offense but could trim a few attempts. Either way he profiles as a mid-pack QB2 for fantasy, worth about 13 to 17 PPR points most weeks.
swingFactors: Whether Arizona's pass defense keeps forcing catch-up volume
How often he keeps forcing deep throws
Interior line health with Gaines out

confidence.note: Seven starts in an unchanged role, backed by a long, consistent career profile.
